title: Function spies
summary: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count.
introduction: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: vi.fn creates a spy that records its calls. You can check the arguments as well as the count.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, vi, beforeEach, afterEach } from "vitest";
test("notifies with score", () => { const notify = vi.fn(); notify(7); expect(notify).toHaveBeenCalledWith(7); });
blocks.title: Function spies

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Check that notify ran exactly once.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A spy should replace a clear boundary, not every line of your own function.
For more detail later, use this [Vitest further reading](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
